CheckTitle: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime has custom JWT authorizer configured for identity propagation
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Runtime Behavior Analysis
Description: **Bedrock AgentCore runtimes** should be configured with a **custom JWT authorizer** and allow the **Authorization header** to propagate end-user identities to downstream tool services, ensuring tool calls are authorized by the originating user and not solely by the agent execution role.
Risk: Without a **custom JWT authorizer** and **Authorization header propagation**, the runtime cannot capture or forward end-user identities to downstream tools. All downstream actions and tool invocations are executed under the **agent execution role**, resulting in confused-deputy risks, lack of granular per-user audit trails, and potential unauthorized access to downstream data.

Code.Other:
1. Open the AWS Console and navigate to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
2. Select **Agent Runtimes** and select the target runtime
3. Under **Authorizer configuration**, enable **Custom JWT Authorizer** and specify OIDC discovery URL, allowed audience, and allowed clients
4. Under **Request header configuration**, add `Authorization` to the **Request header allowlist**
5. Save changes to ensure end-user identity propagation is enabled

Recommendation.Text: Configure a **custom JWT authorizer** on every Bedrock AgentCore runtime and include `Authorization` in the request header allowlist to validate incoming end-user tokens and forward identity context to downstream tool integrations.

Notes: Reports one finding per AgentCore runtime. A runtime whose detail could not be retrieved returns MANUAL rather than PASS/FAIL, preventing false PASS results when permissions are insufficient.
